requirement: Implement AtomicFileOps providing write_text_atomic and write_json_atomic with temp file in target parent dir, fsync durability, atomic replacement, and cleanup on failure.
skeleton: AtomicFileOps class with static methods write_text_atomic and write_json_atomic.

rationale.teaches: Atomic file replacement: a temp file in the target's directory, fsync before rename, os.replace for the swap, and temp-file cleanup on failure.
rationale.why: Every miss writes the correct bytes on the happy path. Only a failure injected mid-write shows a truncated target, a leaked temp file, or a cross-device rename error.

candidates.why_wrong: The target is opened directly for writing, so a failure mid-write leaves a truncated file in place.
The temp file lives in the system temp directory, so the rename can cross filesystems and fail with EXDEV.
fsync is skipped, so the rename can land before the data reaches disk.
The temp file is not removed when writing fails, so each failure leaks a file next to the target.
os.rename is used instead of os.replace, so on Windows an existing target makes the swap fail.
